  "signals_observed": [
    "Alert date: 2025-02-13; merchant_id: 143.",
    "Trigger B: AUP-06.1 breach: 30d chargeback rate 5.7% (3 disputes / 53 orders).",
    "cb_rate_30d: 0.05660377358490566; disputes_30d: 3; orders_30d: 53.",
    "gmv_30d: 2541576 cents; base_gmv: 8720362 cents; base_days: 90; base_orders: 183.",
    "volume_z: -0.9626166822003952; ticket_drift: 1.0063378492340846.",
    "new_gmv_30d: 376837 cents; new_gmv_share: 0.14826902677708634.",
    "refunds_30d: 0; refund_rate_30d: 0.0; base_refunds: 0; base_refund_rate: 0.0.",
    "merchant_age_days: 180; days_since_first_order: 178; cum_orders: 301."
  ],
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "kind": "bustout",
      "likelihood": "med",
      "reasoning": "The reported chargeback breach warrants investigation, but three disputes do not establish coordinated fraud or non-delivery. Negative volume_z and near-unity ticket_drift do not support the sales-ramp pattern; buyer-account quality is unknown."
    },
    {
      "kind": "marketing_push",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "The supplied volume and ticket comparisons show no aggregate spike supporting a marketing-driven alert. Campaign records could nevertheless explain the disputed orders or a localized sales change."
    },
    {
      "kind": "data_issue",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "The reported rate agrees with 3 disputes divided by 53 orders, so there is no visible arithmetic inconsistency. Missing orders, duplicated disputes, or incorrect event attribution remain untested."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "reserve",
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "Inspect the three dispute records for distinct order IDs, reasons, amounts, status, and supporting evidence; reconcile them to processor records available by the alert date.",
    "Check shipment, carrier delivery, and customer communications for disputed orders plus a small recent-order sample. Repeated verified non-delivery would support bust-out; documented fulfillment would weaken it.",
    "Reconcile refund requests and pending or completed refunds against support tickets and processor records; zero recorded refunds does not establish zero customer complaints.",
    "Reconcile the 53 orders and GMV to source transactions, checking ingestion completeness, timestamps, duplicates, and cancellations. Corrected counts could dismiss the metric breach.",
    "Review dated campaign or promotion records and buyer-account histories for recent orders, checking whether legitimate acquisition explains activity or linked thin accounts support coordinated purchasing."
  ],
  "memo_markdown": "Merchant 143 triggered AUP-06.1 on February 13: three disputes across 53 trailing-30-day orders, a 5.66% reported chargeback rate. GMV was 2,541,576 cents. Volume_z is -0.963 and ticket_drift is 1.006; these comparisons do not show the ramp or ticket expansion expected in the described bust-out pattern. Recorded refunds are zero, which does not establish successful fulfillment.\n\nRecommend a provisional payout reserve, with the percentage set by the human reviewer under applicable policy, while completing focused checks. The dispute breach supports caution, but the supplied evidence does not establish bust-out or justify termination.\n\nFirst verify the three dispute records and fulfillment of those orders, then sample recent deliveries, reconcile refund requests, and check campaign records and transaction ingestion. Repeated verified non-delivery alongside linked thin buyer accounts would strengthen bust-out and support considering a settlement pause. Documented delivery, isolated disputes, or a corrected data denominator would weaken the alert and support returning to monitoring."
}
